key_insight: Talk2Move frames text-instructed geometric editing as a sequential decision problem and combines reinforcement learning with a diffusion-based transformer to perform object-level translations, rotations, and resizes from natural language — enabling precise spatial edits with limited paired supervision.
problem_solved: Existing multimodal text-to-image methods can change appearance or style but struggle to perform explicit object-level geometric transformations (translate/rotate/scale) because of scarce paired supervision, ambiguous language grounding, and the need for temporally or spatially coherent actions within scenes.
method: Formulate geometric editing as an RL policy that emits object-centric transformation actions (translate/rotate/scale) conditioned on scene state and a natural-language instruction.

Integrate the learned policy with a diffusion-based transformation/refinement module to produce realistic, spatially coherent edits; training uses sparse rewards (e.g., alignment, IoU, perceptual scores) and self-supervision to reduce reliance on paired data.
Use a scene parser / object grounding module to map language mentions to object slots and constrain the action space, enabling precise per-object manipulation.
impact: Enables more controllable, interpretable text-driven scene editing for applications like image/video editing, AR/VR content creation, and embodied agents — reducing the need for expensive paired datasets while improving spatial reasoning and object-level control.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: language input → scene parser/object detection → RL policy (action sequence) → diffusion-based geometric refinement → edited scene output

paper_title: Talk2Move: Reinforcement Learning for Text-Instructed Object-Level Geometric Transformation in Scenes
paper_authors: Jing Tan, Zhaoyang Zhang, Yantao Shen, Jiarui Cai, Shuo Yang
